items.prompt: Which word is a noun?
hints: A noun names a person, place, animal or thing.
Could you point to it?
Which one could you put a cup on?
items.explanation: Table names a thing, so it is a noun.

options.why: Slowly tells how something is done.

items.prompt: Which word matches the picture?
hints: How many are there?
Box ends with x.
Words that end in x add -es.
items.explanation: There is more than one box. Box ends in x, so we add -es: boxes.

options.why: Words that end in x add -es.

items.prompt: Add -s or -es? Sort the words.
hints: Say each word for more than one.
Words ending in s, ss, x, sh or ch add -es.
Start with bench. Say two benches. Can you hear the extra sound?
items.explanation: Bench, dress and glass add -es. Frog, book and lamp add -s.

items.prompt: Write the plural. 'one baby, two ___'
hints: Baby ends with y.
Look at the letter before the y. It is not a vowel.
Change the y to i, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Baby ends in a consonant and y, so we change y to i and add -es: babies.

items.prompt: Which noun always needs a capital letter?
hints: Names of people and places are special nouns.
They always start with a capital letter.
Which word is the name of a real place?
items.explanation: Jakarta is the name of a city, so it always has a capital letter: Jakarta.

items.prompt: Choose all the nouns. 'The teacher put the books on the desk.'
hints: Three words are nouns.
Look for a person and things.
Ask: who or what is in the sentence?
items.explanation: Teacher, books and desk are nouns. They name a person and things.

items.prompt: Choose the missing word. 'One child, two ___.'
hints: Child does not follow the usual rule.
The word for more than one child is special.
Think: girls and boys together are ___.
items.explanation: The plural of child is children. It is a special plural.

options.why: Child does not just add s.
Children already means more than one.

items.prompt: Match one to more than one.
hints: These words do not add -s.
The middle of the word changes.
Start with man. What do we say for two?
items.explanation: Mouse becomes mice, foot becomes feet, tooth becomes teeth and man becomes men.

items.prompt: Write the plural. 'one lady, three ___'
hints: Lady ends with y.
The letter before y is d, a consonant.
Change y to i, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Lady becomes ladies. We change y to i and add -es.

items.prompt: Sort the nouns. Names, or other nouns?
hints: Names of people, places and days have capital letters.
Other nouns do not need capitals.
Start with Bali. Is it the name of a place?
items.explanation: Bali, Mr Lee and Monday are names, so they have capital letters. Beach, teacher and day are other nouns.

items.prompt: What is the plural of sheep?
hints: Some animal words do not change at all.
Fish is the same for one or many.
Say each choice after the word ten.
items.explanation: Sheep is the same for one and for many: one sheep, ten sheep.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
hints: Three means more than one.
Fox ends with x.
Words that end with x add -es.
items.explanation: Fox ends in x, so the plural is foxes.

options.why: Fox ends in x, so it adds -es.

items.prompt: Fix the plural. 'Two puppys played in the garden.' Write the right word.
hints: Puppy ends with y.
The letter before y is p, a consonant.
Change y to i, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Puppy becomes puppies. We change y to i and add -es.

items.prompt: What is the plural of wolf?
hints: Wolf ends with f.
Think of leaf and leaves.
Change f to v, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Wolf becomes wolves. The f changes to v and we add -es, like leaf and leaves.

options.why: Wolf changes its f before the ending.
Wolf changes its f to v.
There is an e before the s.

items.prompt: Choose all the plurals that end in -ies.
hints: Three words are right.
Look at the letter before the y in the word for one.
Is the letter before y a vowel or not?
items.explanation: Cherry, story and fly change y to ies. Key and boy have a vowel before the y, so they just add s.

options.why: Key ends in a vowel and y, so we just add s.
Boy ends in a vowel and y, so we just add s.

items.prompt: Which word is NOT a plural?
hints: Three words mean more than one.
Some plurals do not end in s.
A word can end in s and still be one thing.
items.explanation: Bus means one bus. Mice, feet and teeth are special plurals.

options.why: Mice is the plural of mouse.
Feet is the plural of foot.
Teeth is the plural of tooth.

items.prompt: How many nouns are in this sentence? 'Grandma gave Raka a mango and a pear.'
hints: Names of people are nouns too.
Look for people and things.
Point to each noun as you count.
items.explanation: Grandma, Raka, mango and pear are nouns. That makes 4.

options.why: Look at the end of the sentence again.
Gave and and are not nouns.

items.prompt: Choose the noun that finishes the sentence. 'I brush my teeth with a ___.'
hints: A noun names a thing.
What do you hold when you brush?
Find the thing, not the action.
items.explanation: Toothbrush is a noun. It names the thing we brush our teeth with.

items.prompt: I can see two ___.
hints: Two means more than one.
Words that end in x add es.
Say each choice aloud. Which one sounds right?
items.explanation: When a word ends in x, we add es to make it plural: one box, two boxes.

items.prompt: Which word is a naming word?
hints: A noun is a person, animal, place or thing.
You can see it.
You eat at it.
items.explanation: Table is a noun.

items.prompt: Which is the plural of box?
hints: More than one box.
After x we add es.
Say the word slowly.
items.explanation: Words that end in x add es, so box becomes boxes.

options.why: Words ending in x add es.

items.prompt: Which is the plural of baby?
hints: The word ends in a consonant and y.
Change the y to i.
Then add es.
items.explanation: Baby becomes babies. We change y to ies.

options.why: Change the y to i first.
Change the y before adding es.

items.prompt: Which is the plural of child?
hints: This word does not just add s.
It changes inside.
Think of a class full of them.
items.explanation: Child becomes children.

items.prompt: Which word is the name of a place?
hints: A place is where you can go.
Think of an island.
It starts with a capital letter.
items.explanation: Bali is the name of a place.

options.why: Rina is the name of a person.

items.prompt: Sort the nouns.
hints: Think about what each noun is.
A person can talk to you.
A place is where you go.
items.explanation: Teacher and farmer are people, goat and rabbit are animals, market and school are places.

items.prompt: Sort the plurals by how they are made.
hints: Look at the ending of each plural.
Think of the word it came from.
Puppies came from puppy.
items.explanation: Cars and bags add s, dishes and buses add es, cities and puppies change y to ies.

items.prompt: Match each word to its plural.
hints: These plurals change inside.
Say each word aloud.
Foot becomes feet.
items.explanation: Each plural is a special one.

items.prompt: Write the plural. One leaf, two ___.
hints: Change the f to v.
Then add es.
Say the word slowly.
items.explanation: Leaf becomes leaves.

items.prompt: Write the plural. One sheep, two ___.
hints: Say it aloud.
This word does not change.
It looks the same.
items.explanation: Sheep stays the same in the plural.

items.prompt: There are three ___ in the garden.
hints: There is more than one.
The word butterfly ends in y.
Change y to ies.
items.explanation: Butterflies is the plural of butterfly.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that stay the same in the plural.
hints: Say the plural of each word.
Two words do not change.
Think of animals.
items.explanation: Sheep and deer stay the same.

items.prompt: Which sentence is right?
hints: Think about the plural of woman.
There is no extra s.
Look at the vowel in the middle of woman.
items.explanation: Women is the plural of woman.

options.text: The two womans went to market.
The two women went to market.
The two womens went to market.
The two woman went to market.
options.why: There are two, so we need the plural.

items.prompt: Label the places.
hints: Say the name of each place.
School is where you learn.
Tap a word, then tap its number.
items.explanation: The pictures show a school, a park and a shop.

figure.alt: A school, a park and a shop.

items.prompt: Complete the table.
hints: Look at the filled row.
Fox ends in x.
Mouse changes inside.
items.explanation: Fox becomes foxes and mouse becomes mice.
head: One
Many
items.caption: One and many
